_what: The Doom Scoop: daily news, usually bad. An ice cream parlour after closing, with the only light in it coming from the dipping cabinet, and a tub in the cabinet for every morning of the last week. Ryan's brief, 2026-09-26. Read by tools/pull-doom-scoop.py, which writes `scoops`, and by tools/make-doom-scoop.py, which draws the room from this file and needs nothing else.
_sources: THE SOURCES ARE RYAN'S, IN THE GROUPS HE PUT THEM IN AND THE ORDER HE LISTED THEM, and nothing in the room re-sorts them: not alphabetically, not by who posted most, not by whose was newest. Picking a news source is a curation decision and it belongs to a person, which is The Feed's rule about its wires. `url` is the address Ryan gave, word for word. `feed` is the one YouTube publishes for that exact list: for a channel link to /videos it is the channel's long-form list (UULF), for a link to /shorts it is the shorts list (UUSH), and a playlist link is that playlist. The channel ids were read off each channel's own page on 2026-09-26 and not typed from memory. A source with no feed is a DOOR: the room links it and scoops nothing from it.
_doors: Ground News and meidasnews.com publish no feed a timer can read. Both were asked on 2026-09-26 at /feed, /rss and /feed.xml: ground.news answered 404 at every one, and meidasnews.com answered 404 or a bot check that asks for JavaScript and no ad blocker. A bot check is somebody saying no to a machine, so nothing here tries to get past it. They are doors on the counter rather than tubs in the cabinet, and the room says so.
_window: AN EDITION IS A MORNING, AND IT IS DATED BY THE MORNING IT WAS SCOOPED: everything published from five in the morning the day before to five that morning, Mountain time, which is the street's own clock: the CB clears at midnight Mountain too. Five and not six because the timer runs at ten past six on whatever clock the laptop is keeping, and on Central time that is ten past five Mountain; an edition has to have closed before the timer that fills it comes round. A morning paper carries yesterday's news for the same reason. An edition whose five o'clock has not come yet is not on the page, however much is in it, because a tub that is still being filled is not a scoop.
_week: A WEEK AND THEN IT IS GONE. The puller keeps the last seven mornings and drops anything older from this file, and the room refuses a scoop older than that. Not archived, not moved to a back page: gone from here, and still on the channel that posted it. The Doomscroll one door along is one roll with no end to it; this is the room with a bottom.
_scoops: WHAT IS TAKEN OFF EACH VIDEO: its id, its title exactly as the channel wrote it, the channel's name as YouTube gives it, when it was published, and how long it runs. Nothing else. Not the description, not the thumbnail, not a count of views, likes or comments. The titles are the channels' own and some of them shout; they are quoted as written, because rewriting somebody's headline is putting words in their mouth. `runs` is lengthSeconds off the video's own watch page, read the same morning, never typed. `state` is what the watch page said: `screen` plays here, `door` plays on YouTube and not in a frame here (its owner switched embedding off, or it is age-gated and shows only to signed-in adults), `pending` is live or not out yet and is asked again next morning, `gone` would not play and is not shown.
_coverage: A CHANNEL'S FEED CARRIES ITS NEWEST UPLOADS AND NO FURTHER BACK, so a channel that posts more between two readings than its feed holds has the earliest of them left off, and nothing can fetch them afterwards from the feed. `covered` records, per source, the stretches of time the feeds have been read all the way through; an edition whose window a source's coverage does not reach all the way across says, on that source, that some of its day may be missing. That is generated, never typed, for check-counts.py's reason.
